description:
## Why

Under Level 3, lint bundle composition uses OSCAL Profile mechanics, not bespoke Rust composition functions. An OSCAL Profile imports one or more Catalogs, selects/excludes Controls, and modifies parameters / status. Profiles can chain.

This means `cabf.br.tls` is an OSCAL Profile importing the workspace's RFC-conformance Catalog (plus possibly a cabf-specific Catalog from `pkix-lint-cabf`), selecting the relevant Controls, setting parameter values (e.g., SC-081 validity caps), and emitting the composed set.

## What

Implement Profile loading + composition:

- Load OSCAL Profile JSON files.
- Resolve imports (a Profile can import other Profiles or Catalogs).
- Apply select/exclude directives (`include-controls`, `exclude-controls`).
- Apply modify directives (`set-parameters`, `adds` to control parts).
- Resolve to an effective Catalog (the 'resolved profile catalog' in OSCAL terms).
- Execute lints against the resolved Catalog.

Composition examples that must work:

1. **Plain Profile**: import RFC-conformance Catalog, select a subset of controls, run lints.
2. **Layered Profile**: cabf.br.tls Profile imports both the RFC Catalog and a cabf-extensions Catalog, selects from each, sets cabf-specific parameter values.
3. **Override Profile**: a customer Profile imports cabf.br.tls Profile and disables one specific control (their organisational deviation).

This replaces any need for Rust functions like `combine_profiles`, `disable_lint`, etc. — those operations become OSCAL Profile directives.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Profile loader + resolver supports import, include-controls, exclude-controls, set-parameters.
- [ ] At least three example Profiles ship as test fixtures, covering the three composition examples above.
- [ ] Composed Profile execution yields the expected lint set + parameter values.
- [ ] Documentation in pkix-lint rustdoc explains the OSCAL Profile composition mechanism and points users at the OSCAL Profile schema for advanced use.

## Out of scope

- Full OSCAL Profile semantics (alterations across all OSCAL field types, custom set-parameter contexts, etc.) — implement only what the workspace's Profile use cases require.
- Profile authoring tools — consumers can hand-write OSCAL Profile JSON or use external OSCAL authoring tools.

## Depends on

PKIX-9vnx.6 (Lint-as-Control mapping — Profiles operate on Controls).
notes:
Reframed 2026-05-11 (Arch 2 — see PKIX-ztmr / PKIX-9vnx notes):

- Profile composition mechanics unchanged (OSCAL Profile semantics: import/select/exclude/modify) — Arch 2 doesn't change *what* we do, just *how* we represent it in Rust.
- Loader walks OSCAL Profile JSON. Resolver applies imports/select/exclude/set-parameters directives. Output: an 'effective Catalog' — internally a Vec<&dyn Lint> + a parameter-override map (or similar), NOT an `oscal::Catalog` Rust type.
- The OSCAL Profile JSON is the canonical authoring format. The Rust runtime walks JSON; it doesn't deserialize it into a Rust mirror first.
- Test fixtures remain as OSCAL Profile JSON files. Acceptance criteria unchanged.
- No longer blocked by PKIX-9vnx.2 (closed).
title: Profile composition via OSCAL Profile semantics (select/exclude/modify, import chaining)
